summary.text: A 58-year-old Caucasian man was diagnosed with multiple myeloma in early 2014. He received induction chemotherapy with dexamethasone, cisplatin, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide and etoposide, pretransplant VDT-Mel chemotherapy with melphalan 200 mg/m^(2), and tandem autologous stem cell transplantation in June and September 2014. He was seropositive for T. gondii before transplant, and antimicrobial prophylaxis consisted of fluconazole, acyclovir and ciprofloxacin.

He was neutropenic for about seven days after both transplants, with prolonged lymphopenia. Following engraftment on day +17 after the second transplant he developed low-grade fevers, headaches and impaired memory. MRI showed a new thalamic lesion with edema, mass effect and faint peripheral enhancement. CSF showed elevated protein, normal glucose and a lymphocyte-predominant WBC count of 94/µL; cytology showed no tumor cells, and blood cultures and the other infectious tests were negative. CSF and serum toxoplasma PCR were positive, establishing toxoplasma encephalitis.

He was empirically started on sulfadiazine and pyrimethamine with leucovorin, developed crystal nephropathy with renal failure while on sulfadiazine, and was changed to clindamycin and pyrimethamine for 8 weeks. Response was favorable at 1-month follow-up. He was then switched to pyrimethamine, leucovorin and atovaquone as secondary prophylaxis during ongoing maintenance chemotherapy. The myeloma progressed, and he died 30 months after HSCT due to progressive myeloma with no evidence of toxoplasmosis.
